claims.finding: Cognyte announced three customer awards inside its 1 May - 31 July quarter - ~$5m (APAC national security upgrade, 2026-05-20), ~$5m (APAC national security agency, 2026-06-25) and ~$15m (APAC military intelligence customer expanding an existing partnership, 2026-07-28) - roughly $25m of disclosed awards, or about 5.6% of the maintained $448m FY27 revenue guide, with the largest of the three landing three days before the quarter closed; the stock nonetheless fell 7.9% over the trailing 20 sessions and sits 30.8% below its 52-week high.

claims.why_not_priced: Each award was a company press release, so it is technically wire copy - but this capture contains zero captured news items, zero analyst notes and no sell-side preview for CGNT across all six sweeps, the stock trades roughly $4.5m a day on a 533k 20-day volume, and the digest's own participants say things like 'can't believe no one talks about this company' and 'glad this is under the radar'. If the disclosed order flow were being priced, the 20-day run-in would not be negative, and the $15m award of 28 July - the largest single disclosure in the six-month series that also includes $10m+ on 03/04 and $20m+ over three years on 04/29 - would have left a mark on the tape rather than none.
claims.independence: The same digest is also the only source, so within this corpus this is a single cluster. The one supporting item from a different file is the filings index: filings.json shows no 6-K, 424B or equity filing between the 2026-07-29 6-K (the routine end-of-July filing that matches the 2025-07-30 analogue by filer-agent document name) and the 2026-09-01 earnings-date 6-K, so nothing offsetting was disclosed in the run-in. none beyond that.
